Our Institution

TTC de la Salle Byumba is a Teacher Training College located in Byumba, Northern Province, Rwanda. Operated by the De La Salle Brothers, we are committed to excellence in teacher education, forming future educators equipped with knowledge, values, and 21st‑century skills.

Life at TTC de la Salle Byumba

Teaching Hearts · Teaching Minds · Transforming Lives

Our Mission

Mission

Enriched by the Lasallian Catholic tradition, TTC De La Salle awakens, nurtures, empowers and transforms preservice teachers to ethical lives of societal service and leadership.

Vision

To be an outstanding hub of the needed Rwandan teachers whose life of faith, fraternity, service and leadership — which are directed toward the common good — will become society's defining features.

Smart Classroom Initiative

This portal is the heart of our Smart Classroom Resource Manager — a live digital ecosystem connecting REB eLearning progress tracking, student attendance with room-level precision, library and resource booking, and a shared photo and video gallery, all in one platform. Students can register themselves from any device, anywhere, and their information reaches every classroom and every teacher instantly. Built for TTC De La Salle Byumba to keep teaching, tracking, and reporting connected in real time — on any computer, at any time.

TTC Programme Reform — 2026/27

TTC training extended from 3 to 5 years

The Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) has announced that, from the 2026/27 academic year (starting 7 September 2026), students newly enrolling in Year One at Teacher Training Colleges follow a five-year teacher-training programme. The change responds to the limited time the three-year programme left for pedagogy and practical classroom experience, and brings Rwanda closer to regional standards for primary teachers.

OLD PROGRAMME
3 years

Led to an A2-level teaching qualification. Officials explained that its packed academic curriculum left too little time for pedagogy and practical classroom experience.

NEW PROGRAMME
5 years

Leads first to a Diploma in Education, with more professional preparation and teaching practice for new Year One students from 2026/27.

What has changed in the academic programme?
AreaWhat the reform means
DurationFive years instead of three for new entrants
Teaching methodologyGreater emphasis on pedagogy and effective teaching methods
Classroom managementMore preparation for managing learners and classroom behaviour
Child developmentGreater attention to learners’ developmental needs
Teaching practiceMore school-based practical experience
Professional studiesMore time for the foundations and professional responsibilities of teaching
QualificationFirst phase moves from an A2 certificate to a Diploma in Education, with a longer-term goal of a bachelor’s-level qualification
The three specialisation areas
AREA 1
Mathematics and Science Education
Preparation to teach mathematics and science concepts using effective teaching methods and practical activities.
AREA 2
Social Sciences and Language Education
Preparation in language learning, communication and social-science subjects.
AREA 3
Early Childhood and Lower Primary Education (ECLPE)
Preparation to teach young children, with attention to foundational literacy, numeracy, child development and school readiness.

Good to know

These are the three broad areas reported for the revised programme; they are not a complete list of modules or subjects. The reform applies to new Year One entrants, and the arrangements for the final two years (at TTCs or at the University of Rwanda College of Education) were still being finalised when it was announced. For official details, always refer to the documents issued by MINEDUC and REB.

Sources: MINEDUC · The New Times (August 2026)

Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy explains how the Smart Classroom Portal / TTC eLearning Monitor collects, uses and protects user information.

Last updated: 18 October 2026

Introduction

This Privacy Policy explains what information the Smart Classroom Portal / TTC eLearning Monitor of TTC de la Salle Byumba collects, why, who can see it and how it is protected. By using the website you agree to this policy.

Information we collect

  • Account details: name, SDMS code, class and stream, role (student, tutor, administrator, librarian) and, for staff, username.
  • Learning records: attendance, test and examination answers, marks and grades, the times you started and submitted, and the exam activity log (for example leaving the page or full screen).
  • Files: files you upload as answers and materials that tutors attach to exams.
  • Forms and library records: messages sent through the Contact Us form, and library borrowing and returning records.
  • Technical information: the browser and device information that is normal for any website, and small items kept on your own device (see below).

How we use the information

  • To let you sign in and to show you only what is meant for your class and role.
  • To run tests and examinations, mark them, give feedback and report results to tutors and administrators.
  • To record attendance and library activity and to run school administration.
  • To answer your messages and to keep the website working and secure.

Marking with artificial intelligence

When a tutor uses AI-assisted marking for essay questions, the question and the student's answer text are sent to an AI service (Google Gemini) from the tutor's computer. Your name and SDMS code are not sent. AI marks are provisional and are reviewed by the tutor.

Who can see your information

  • Your tutors see the results, answers, files and activity log of the classes they teach. Administrators can see all records.
  • Other students cannot see your results or files.
  • Data is stored with our cloud service provider (Google Firebase) so that the system works on every device.

Data sharing

We do not sell your personal data. We share it only with authorised school staff for educational and administrative purposes, with the service providers needed to run the website, or when the law requires it.

Data stored on your device

To keep you signed in and to sign in faster, your browser may store your session, a scrambled (not readable) copy of your password check and your class details. A tutor's computer may also store the AI key. Sign out on shared computers and use your browser's settings to clear this data.

Security

Passwords are stored in scrambled form and connections use secure protocols. Accounts are signed out automatically after a period of inactivity. No system is completely secure, so keep your password private and tell us at once if you suspect misuse.

How long we keep information

Results and attendance are kept for school records for as long as the school needs them. Files uploaded for an exam may be deleted after the exam is finished. You can ask your tutor or administrator to correct wrong information.

Children's privacy

This website is for education. Learners under 18 use it under the supervision of the school, and the school collects their information only to teach, assess and administer their studies.

Changes to this policy

We may update this Privacy Policy and will post the new version on this page. When the Terms or this policy change, you will be asked to agree again.

Terms of Use

These Terms of Use govern access to and use of the Smart Classroom Portal / TTC eLearning Monitor website of TTC de la Salle Byumba, including CBT Exams, Gallery, Videos, Attendance, Library and the other services on it.

Last updated: 18 October 2026

1. Acceptance of these Terms

By opening or using this website you confirm that you have read, understood and agree to these Terms of Use and to the Privacy Policy. Anyone who wishes to use the website (students, tutors, administrators, librarians and visitors) must accept them first. If you do not agree, you must not use the website. Learners under 18 should use the website under the supervision of a teacher, parent or guardian.

2. Who may use the website

The website is for the learners, staff and authorised visitors of TTC de la Salle Byumba. Students sign in only with their own SDMS code, class and stream. Staff accounts are for school work only.

3. Accounts and passwords

  • Keep your password secret. Do not share it and do not use another person's account or SDMS code.
  • You are responsible for everything done with your account. Tell your tutor or administrator at once if you think someone else knows your password.
  • Sign out when you finish, especially on a shared computer. For security, sessions are signed out automatically after 10 minutes without activity (never while an exam is in progress).
  • A student's password is created the first time they sign in. An administrator can reset it.

4. Permitted use

  • Reading, downloading and using educational materials, videos, photos and documents for learning.
  • Taking tests and examinations that are set for your own class and stream.
  • Sharing school resources inside the school community only.

5. Online tests and examinations (CBT)

  • Do your own work. Cheating, copying, getting help from other people, impersonating another student or sharing questions or answers is not allowed.
  • An exam can be opened only during the time set by the tutor and only by students of the class it is set for. The timer keeps running even if you refresh the page, and the exam is submitted automatically when time is up.
  • You can be signed in to an exam on one device at a time. Opening it on another device signs the first one out.
  • The system records activity during an exam, for example leaving the exam page or full screen, and shows it to your tutors.
  • Objective questions are marked automatically. Essay marks may be assisted by artificial intelligence and are provisional until your tutor reviews them. The tutor's and the school's decision on marks is final.
  • Breaking these rules can lead to the exam being cancelled and to disciplinary action under school rules.

6. Materials and files you upload

  • Tutors may attach images, documents and links to an exam. Students may upload their own answer files where the tutor allows it.
  • Upload only your own work, in the allowed file types (images, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, text), up to the size and number limits shown (1.5 MB per file).
  • Do not upload viruses, offensive or unlawful material, or work that belongs to someone else.
  • Tutors and administrators can view, download and delete uploaded files. Old exam files may be deleted from the system after an exam is finished. Keep your own copy of anything important.

7. Prohibited use

  • Trying to access another person's account, marks or data, or to bypass the security or the limits of the website.
  • Copying, selling, changing or distributing site content without permission.
  • Uploading harmful files, malware or offensive material.
  • Using forms for spam or unrelated messages, harassing others, or using automated tools to access or overload the website.
  • Using the website for anything unlawful.

8. Your work and our content

Videos, documents, photos and resources on this website belong to the school unless stated otherwise. You keep the ownership of your own work, but by submitting it you allow the school to store it, show it to your tutors and administrators, mark it, and keep the results for educational and administrative purposes.

9. Records and privacy

The school keeps records such as your name, SDMS code, class and stream, attendance, test results, uploaded files and the exam activity log. These are used only for teaching, assessment and school administration, as explained in the Privacy Policy. When an essay answer is marked with artificial intelligence, only the question and the answer text (never your name or SDMS code) are sent to the AI service.

10. Availability and accuracy

The website is provided as it is, for educational use. It may be slow, unavailable or contain mistakes, for example because of internet or power problems. We try to keep it working but do not promise it will always be available or error-free. We are not responsible for external links or third-party content.

11. Limitation of responsibility

To the extent allowed by law, the school and the people who run this website are not responsible for loss or damage caused by using, or not being able to use, the website, including loss of data or work because of device, internet or power failure.

12. Suspension and termination

The school may refuse, restrict or suspend access, cancel an exam attempt, or remove content if these Terms are broken or if this is needed to protect the website or other users. Serious cases may be reported to the school administration.

13. Changes to these Terms

We may update these Terms. When they change, everyone must agree to the new version before continuing to use the website. Continuing to use the website after you agree means you accept the Terms that applied at that time.

14. Questions and governing law

For questions, use the Contact Us form on this website or speak to the school administration. These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Rwanda.
